  16 rewiring_a_running_world (REWRITTEN TWICE, 2026-08-03. Draft 1
     wrapped add_spell_to_contract in a `with conduit.transaction(...)`
     window - the literal thing AGENTS.md rules against. Draft 2 removed
     the window but was still a lesson ABOUT the transaction plane.
     OWNER RULING: transactions must not leak out of the base code at
     all - they are not curriculum vocabulary, and `conduit.link` is
     what you use. So the subject changed, not just the code: this is
     now a lesson about CHANGING THE WIRING WHILE THE WORLD RUNS -
     link, pull, meld - in which the machinery is never named.
     WHAT IT TEACHES: each structural verb is COMPLETE IN ITSELF, so
     there is nothing to open, hold or commit; SHARING IS A PULL and the
     conduit NAMED in add_spell_to_contract must OWN the spell (an
     owner-push is refused); the five-step order of operations per
     dependency edge; and the two link() refusals, braked-posture before
     not-dynamic, so ALLOWED-to-do is checked before WHAT-IT-IS.
     Concurrency appears as one plain sentence - independent work
     overlaps, and a collision names the holder rather than hanging.
     WHAT WAS CUT AND WHY IT WAS RIGHT TO CUT: claim modes, scope keys
     vs hashes, admission waits. All true, all internal. Teaching them
     invites a reader to reach for them.
     (Retained here for maintainers only, since the map is not a
     lesson: "Readers (meld paths)
     NEVER ENTER THIS PLANE; they remain protected by validity gating
     that commits trigger." meld() takes no transaction and appears
     nowhere in the admission vocabulary - the plane serializes
     STRUCTURAL MUTATION only. Most systems that grow a transaction
     manager eventually drag reads into it and find out their throughput
     WAS the lock. PUBLIC DOOR: Conduit.transaction /
     begin_transaction / end_transaction, all marked `Public API`; the
     context form ends with success=False on exception, so a crash
     aborts rather than half-committing. SCOPE KEYS DECLARE SCOPE;
     SCOPE HASHES DECLARE NOTHING - one line apart in the same
     signature, and the docstring says outright that hashes "carry NO
     claims... buy no isolation". A silent-failure trap that documents
     itself. THREE MODES: x excludes everything, s/s coexist, ix/ix
     coexist, and unspecified defaults to x so modes are an opt-in to
     MORE concurrency. THE `ix` DESIGN IS THE STEALABLE PART: owning
     spellbooks are claimed ix rather than x, so two agents doing
     additive piece-work (bind, link, cluster) on one spellbook never
     wait on each other, while transfer_ownership takes x on the whole
     thing and excludes both. You are not locking an object, you are
     declaring what you intend to do to it. WAITING IS BOUNDED in slices
     of min(remaining, 1.0) - the slicing caps the cost of a release
     landing between an attempt and the park at one second instead of
     the whole deadline - and the timeout RAISES WITH BLOCKING SCOPE
     KEYS AND HOLDER REQUEST IDS. One root-admission knob only:
     max_transaction_wait_time_in_seconds, on the frame posture.
     AND THE SEVEN BRAKES GATE FAMILIES BY NAME, checked before
     admission is attempted, with a different sentence from the
     dynamic-mode refusal: what a world IS is not the same fact as what
     it has been ALLOWED TO DO)

  17 notch_swapping_a_live_object (LINEAGES AND THE STAGING HALF. bind
     -> bind_inactive (park a candidate on the SAME index, selection
     unchanged) -> notch_spell (repoint the selection). THE FIRST TWO
     ARE USER SURFACE AND THE THIRD IS NOT DRIVEN BY HAND - notch_spell
     takes the parked OBJECT, which lives in the Spellbook's private
     parking lot, and the Spellbook is not what you notch from. The
     lesson stops at that boundary and demonstrates it (a parked id
     resolves to the ACTIVE member) instead of poking through it.
     WHAT STAGING BUYS: the expensive, failure-prone half of a swap -
     compiling, registering and owning the new version - happens while
     the old version is still serving, because a parked candidate is
     inert and unmeldable. Preparing a swap and taking it are two acts.
     AN INDEX IS A VERSION LINEAGE
     WITH ONE SELECTED MEMBER, so a notch creates, binds and removes
     NOTHING - the outgoing version stays in the lineage and stays
     resolvable by id. THAT is why ROLLBACK IS JUST A NOTCH THE OTHER
     WAY: no undo log, no snapshot restore, because nothing was thrown
     away. THE OWNERSHIP SPLIT: the CONDUIT admits the transaction (it
     owns the change-control envelope and the links), the SPELLBOOK
     applies the switch (it owns the index maps), and neither half is
     callable alone - Spellbook exposes no public notch verb at all.
     FOUR THINGS MAKE A LIVE SWAP SAFE: the notch strategy's on_start
     QUIESCES the sealed conduits' CreationGates so no in-flight meld
     straddles the repoint; tearing down the outgoing creation context
     BUMPS THE DOOR EPOCH so the warm fast-door cannot serve the stale
     spell; the index is re-registered DIRTY so revalidation is lazy and
     the window stays short; and the whole switch runs under one seal
     (maintainer detail, deliberately unnamed in the lesson itself, the
     same way 16 no longer names it). BORROWERS ARE FANNED
     OUT AND THE TWO KINDS GET DIFFERENT ANSWERS: a version-anchored
     borrower has its copy PARKED, an index-link receiver has its head
     MOVED - never-substitute at the topology grain, where whoever named
     a version keeps that version's fate and whoever named a lineage
     follows the lineage. FOOTGUN: change_reason defaults to
     `selected_different_spell`, which records an ordinary selection and
     MISATTRIBUTES a mutation in the state history)

  18 the_package_reads_itself_to_you (THE TIER FINALE, and it ends where
     an agent BEGINS. Four views hang off the package root and answer AT
     IMPORT - queryable with no Spellbook, no Conduit, no conjured
     anything. Two are `SystemDocumentView` (__architecture__,
     __components__); two are `SystemGraphView` (__graph_network__,
     __graph_details__), which SUBCLASSES it - so the graph documents
     answer every prose question and add nodes and edges on top.
     THE THESIS: YOU DO NOT PAGE A SYSTEM DOCUMENT, YOU ADDRESS IT.
     `addressing` publishes what keys MEAN - "section" (heading paths)
     or "source_path" (repo-relative files) - so a caller asks the shape
     instead of inferring it from a sample and silently missing.
     THE CHEAP SURVEY, THEN THE PAID READ: keys() / groups(depth) /
     index() cost no document text, and index() returns
     Section(key, start_line, end_line, line_count) - sizing PER
     SECTION. find() addresses by key; search() investigates BODIES,
     ranked by hit count with a preview. Two different questions,
     neither costing you the document. Only then get(key) or
     reader(key, ...).
     `reader()` TAKING A KEY IS THE WHOLE DESIGN - the cursor is scoped
     to a SECTION, so an agent that narrowed correctly never pages the
     document at all.
     CITATIONS, NOT PARAPHRASES: cite(key) -> "src_graph.md:3518-3596",
     cite(key, line=) -> "src_graph.md:3520". An agent hands back an
     address a human can open and check. That is a falsifiable answer,
     which a summary is not - the best thing in the API.
     REFUSED IS NOT MISSING: available / reason / verify(). A document
     that fails verification still EXISTS and still answers, because
     omitting it would make a stale index look identical to a document
     that never shipped - and the second invites an agent to invent.
     verify() is ALWAYS False for an unavailable document; there is
     nothing to check.)

  19 the_codebase_as_a_walkable_graph (18 addressed prose; the two GRAPH
     documents carry that whole surface AND a real graph, answered at
     import with nothing conjured. THE MOVE WORTH REMEMBERING:
     `node_at(source_path, line)` turns a traceback line into the NODE
     that encloses it, and `impact()` turns that node into a blast
     radius - stack trace to affected files without leaving the process.
     EVERY EDGE EXPLAINS ITSELF: Edge carries `why` (the justification,
     travelling WITH the edge) and `origin` - `authored` or `derived`,
     i.e. did a human assert this or did a tool infer it. `origin` is a
     TRUST FILTER accepted by walk() and impact(), so you can traverse
     only what someone meant, or only what a machine can prove. A graph
     that cannot separate the two forces you to trust all of it equally,
     which in practice means trusting none of it. AND GUESSES DO NOT
     SHIP - edge_count excludes extractor candidates, which over-
     generate ~8x and are leads, not evidence.
     `walk()` YIELDS, and that is a context-budget decision in the same
     family as 18's paging: a generator "so an agent can stop at the
     first useful hop instead of materialising a subgraph it will
     discard", breadth-first so stopping early stops at the RIGHT
     things. TWO GUARANTEES MAKE IT SAFE: cycles are handled (`borrows`
     and `used_by` run both ways, every node expanded at most once, an
     unguarded walk would not terminate), and AN EDGE TO AN UNKNOWN NODE
     IS STILL YIELDED then not expanded - "the relationship is real even
     where the target is not described here", so the graph never
     understates what touches what. IMPACT IS MEASURED IN FILES, ranked
     by proximity: not 400 symbols, but the files in the order you
     should open them. AND THE PAIR JOINS - details_key(node_id) /
     describe(node_id) address prose in the OTHER document, which is why
     the two ship together)

  20 the_workstation_an_agents_workbench (advanced 12 introduced the
     workstation as a STORE; this is what it is FOR. THE LOOP:
     bind_object -> set_target -> execute_target_method(...,
     bind_as_name="result") -> set_target("result"). A COMMAND'S RETURN
     VALUE BECOMES THE NEXT NAMED BINDING, so an agent works in steps it
     named itself instead of carrying objects in its head or re-deriving
     them from the runtime every call. THREE STORES, one namespace each -
     the same name in `objects` and `attributes` is not a collision, and
     describe_bindings() reports FIVE keys because the fifth,
     `target_store`, names WHICH store the active target came from so a
     target round-trips through get(name, store=...). STRONG VS WEAK IS
     ENFORCED: explicit weak on a non-weakreferenceable value RAISES
     rather than storing it strongly, because a silent degrade pins an
     object the caller believed was collectable. AND A COLLECTED WEAK
     BINDING PUBLISHES A ROOM EVENT - "what I was holding went away" is
     TOLD, not discovered by dereferencing a hole. TWO WAYS TO STOP
     POINTING: clear_target() deselects and the object lives;
     cleanup_target() calls cleanup ON it first. Putting the tool down
     vs dismantling it.
     THE SECURITY LINE, WORTH KNOWING WHICH SIDE YOU ARE ON: the command
     system gates runtime access BEFORE a bind and leaves already-bound
     workstation objects OUTSIDE post-bind ACL policing. Getting the
     handle is the checkpoint; using it is not re-litigated per call.
     AND THE WORKSTATION NEVER FABRICATES - it holds room-local bindings
     only, resolution stays the command system's job, and cleanup()
     clears the stores while deliberately NOT cleaning the objects in
     them, because it did not make them.
     (execute_target_method lives on the base CommandSystem and is NOT
     overridden by CodegenCommandSystem - verified by AST - so the
     workbench loop is available in every room kind that has a command
     system at all.)
     TWO RUN NOTES, both refusals the author had assumed away, both now
     the best moments in the lesson:
       - `get_target()` on an empty bench RAISES ValueError; it does not
         return None. None would be a VALUE, and a caller would call a
         method on it before noticing.
       - `get(name)` with no `store=` REFUSES AS AMBIGUOUS once the name
         exists in two stores. The stores do not collide on WRITE and
         are deliberately NOT merged on READ. The lesson now shows the
         SAME bare call succeeding earlier and refusing later: nothing
         about the call changed, the world did. A bare name is only an
         address while it happens to be unique, and melder says so the
         moment it stops being one.

  21 many_agents_writing_code_at_once (the shape melder is actually
     built for - four agents, four rooms, one shared world, concurrent.
     HOW DATA LEAVES GENERATED CODE: the executor runs the source in a
     controlled namespace and lifts exactly ONE name out of it -
     `CodegenExecutionResult` is constructed with `result=` taken from
     the namespace after the code runs, so `payload["result"]` is the
     whole boundary. Everything else the code computed dies with the
     sandbox. One value out means the boundary is a VALUE, not a scope
     an agent can leak through.
     THE PAYLOAD IS A VERDICT, NOT A RETURN VALUE: `accepted` and
     `frame_name` always present; `reason`, `runtime_error`,
     `validation_issues`, `result` fill in per outcome. The SAME shape
     describes a refusal, a crash and a success, so an agent branches on
     `accepted` rather than catching (expert 12's law, now load-bearing
     across four threads).
     FOUR AGENTS, FOUR ROOMS, ONE WORLD: each opens its own rift and
     therefore its own room, workstation and memory; what they share is
     the target frame. PRIVATE BENCHES, SHARED WORLD - asserted by
     distinct workstation ids.
     WHAT IS NOT SERIALIZED: nothing here opens a transaction, because
     computing a value mutates no structure. Four agents run genuinely
     in parallel and none waits. The plane only arbitrates when one of
     them binds or links - and even then the vocabulary stays out of the
     agent's code.
     PER-AGENT AUDIT IS FREE: subscribe to one room's memory, run the
     identical call in two, and the other room's call is absent. It
     falls out of per-agent rooms rather than being a feature anyone
     built.
     The four job sources were EXECUTED in a restricted namespace during
     authoring to confirm their expected values - generated source in a
     lesson is still source, and asserting its output without running it
     is the same mistake as asserting an API without reading it.)

  22 asking_what_code_would_do_before_running_it (FORESIGHT, and the
     codegen room's centerpiece. `research_preview(code,
     against_spell_id=, frame_name=)` answers FIVE questions in one
     call: what the candidate DEFINES and IMPORTS (from its AST), the
     would-be source + structural DIFF against the version it would
     replace, the IMPACT of that replacement joined with research
     residency, its candidate_sha256, and - only when frame_name is
     given - the room's normal codegen VALIDATION verdict. So "may I"
     and "what would happen" are answered together instead of being two
     round trips.
     ORDER OF SETUP IS LOAD-BEARING AND EASY TO GET WRONG: a bind
     auto-records into research ONLY if the root is already live. The
     seam returns quietly when research is absent, cleaned or inactive,
     because "research bookkeeping never gates a bind" - so a world
     built before you activate research is a world research never saw.
     Activate custody and record FIRST, then build. And the impact half
     reaches through the Crystallizer, so it refuses loudly without live
     custody (expert 14's record-vs-foresight split).
     THE READ-ONLY CLAIM IS CHECKED, NOT TRUSTED: the lesson snapshots
     research_heads() before and after the preview and asserts they are
     IDENTICAL, then re-melds to show the live object is unchanged.
     "Nothing executes, binds, or records" is melder's claim about
     itself; the lesson makes it an assertion.
     AND A BROKEN CANDIDATE ANSWERS RATHER THAN EXPLODING - source that
     does not parse comes back with `parse_error` populated and the
     payload otherwise shaped the same. An agent's generator emits
     garbage sometimes, and a foresight tool that raised on garbage
     would fail exactly when it is needed most)

  23 branching_the_record_and_joining_back (research lanes are melder's
     branches, and they look like git until three places where they
     deliberately are not.
     A BRANCH STARTS EMPTY. `create_lane(attach_to=, attach_at_spell_id=)`
     records ANCESTRY ONLY - no node copied, no node moved, anchor lane
     untouched, new lane at zero versions with a memory of where it came
     from. A git branch starts AT a commit and carries the history; this
     one starts at nothing and remembers a point.
     ANCHORING IS ALL-OR-NOTHING - both arguments or neither, and
     exactly one raises BEFORE the lock is taken. No "anchor to the
     current tip" shorthand exists, because the anchor is the one fact
     the join later reasons about and a shorthand would let you record a
     different anchor than you meant.
     THE DEFAULT LANE TYPE IS `experiment`, NOT the default lane's
     `development` - the safe classification is the one you get by not
     thinking about it.
     AND THE JOIN IS DIVERGENCE-AWARE, which is the lesson: the CLEAN
     path needs the source anchored onto the receiver AND the receiver's
     tip STILL AT that anchor. Anything else refuses, and THE REFUSAL
     NAMES BOTH TIPS. `force=True` is an EXPLICIT SUPERSEDE and melder
     says plainly what it is not: "Reconciliation-by-content is not a
     join concern: compose in the codegen workshop, register the
     multi-parent result, then join." A VCS that merges FOR you is
     guessing at your source; this one refuses to. `collapse` chooses
     whether the full line or only the tip comes across, residence
     travels with whatever moves, and a joined source accepts no further
     work.)

  24 loading_a_whole_world_back (the round trip. FIVE VERBS AND ONLY THE
     LAST IS A BOOT: create_checkpoint -> describe_checkpoint ->
     flush_checkpoint -> reload_cached_checkpoint -> load_checkpoint.
     The first four move a RECORD around; `load_checkpoint` unfolds it
     into the live runtime.
     A RESTORE IS NOT A RESURRECTION. The RestoreReport carries status,
     built counts, SHORTFALL ENTRIES, and an IDENTITY TRANSLATION MAP -
     old id -> new id. Rebuilt objects get NEW identities, so the world
     that comes back is EQUIVALENT, not identical, and anything holding
     a raw pre-restore id is holding a stale address. The map is the
     only honest way to translate one.
     SHORTFALLS ARE NAMED, NOT DROPPED - a class that can no longer be
     imported becomes an entry rather than a silent omission, because a
     restore that quietly dropped what it could not rebuild would look
     identical to a world that never had those things (expert 18's law
     at the boot grain).
     CHECKPOINTS ACCUMULATE and list_checkpoint_ids() returns them in
     exact ledger creation order - there is no "the" checkpoint.
     And md.CrystallizerBootstrap is the operator's one-call form of the
     same sequence, with one knob, `with_preflight_gate`, that is an
     ACCEPTED NO-OP and says so in its own docstring instead of quietly
     doing nothing.)

  25 many_research_sets_one_world (research sets, PLURAL - every earlier
     lesson used the default and never mentioned there was a choice.
     A SET IS THE WORLD A LANE LIVES IN: own lanes, own residency, own
     journal, own campaigns. Two sets are two independent investigations
     of the SAME runtime, so expert 23's join can never cross them and a
     lane name in one says nothing about a lane name in the other - two
     agents auditing one world for different reasons need not share a
     vocabulary or know about each other.
     THE CRUX: a version can be RESIDENT in one set and UNKNOWN to
     another, and neither is wrong. A set records what an investigation
     CHOSE to look at, not everything that exists.
     AN UNKNOWN SET NAME RAISES AND THE ERROR LISTS THE KNOWN ONES -
     small, and enormous for an agent: a typo self-corrects instead of
     returning an empty set that reads as "this world has no history".
     And the bare `research_set()` is THE DEFAULT, never ALL - the cheap
     call is scoped rather than sweeping.
     AUTHORING NOTE: the first draft used `list_lanes()` and
     `heads_view()` behind hasattr guards. NEITHER EXISTS. The guards
     would have hidden that at runtime, which is the guessing pattern
     this tier keeps relearning - rewritten on `walk(lane_ref)`, which
     returns a LIST of self-describing node payloads, not a dict.)

THE THROUGH-LINES, AT EXPERT GRAIN (both inherited from advanced)

  TWO BITS, NEVER ONE
      11  eligible to be targeted / actually attached
      14  a composition EXISTS / it is the CURRENT one for its lane
      15  a stamp is SET / a record inherited it
  Presence never implies liveness, and reach never implies grant.

  MELDER NEVER SUBSTITUTES
      10  a typo'd override path REFUSES; it does not hit the nearest
          socket, and at depth four that would be undetectable
      12  a rejected validation returns a VERDICT; it does not run a
          safer version of your code
      14  a rediscovery REFUSES; you cannot end up with two names for
          one subsystem
      14  a foresight read with no live custody REFUSES; it does not
          return an empty report that reads like "nothing found"
      15  an empty campaign REFUSES ON THE WRITE because the READ cannot
          address it
  The 15 case is the sharpest statement of it in the library: melder
  would rather fail your write than let you create a fact that nobody
  can ever ask a question about.

  THIRD THROUGH-LINE, VISIBLE ONLY AT THIS TIER - ABSENCE IS TYPED
  Advanced 15 taught it on the read surface (hidden vs empty, and the
  probe that tells them apart). Expert repeats it at three more grains,
  and the shape is identical every time: melder gives the two kinds of
  nothing two different spellings.
      11  "not allowed by policy" vs "rift_enabled is False" - refused
          by the OBSERVER, or refused by the WORLD
      12  ValueError on a malformed REQUEST vs a verdict object on
          disallowed CODE
      14  a refusal when custody is off vs unknown_custody_members when
          custody is on and the member simply has none
      16  "requires dynamic mode" vs "disabled for the current frame
          posture" - what a world IS vs what it is ALLOWED to do
  If you only ever learn one thing from this tier, learn to ask which
  KIND of nothing you are holding.

  FOURTH THROUGH-LINE, AND 16 IS WHERE IT BECOMES OBVIOUS -
  DECLARE INTENT, NOT POSSESSION
      14  a composition names a SET so you can ask about the set
      15  a campaign names an EFFORT so work can be attributed to it
      16  a claim mode names WHAT YOU INTEND TO DO to a scope, which is
          why `ix` and `ix` coexist where `x` and `x` cannot
  In all three the system gets more useful the more precisely you say
  what you mean, and melder's half of the bargain is that it never
  guesses on your behalf when you were vague - it refuses and names the
  ambiguity. Expert 10's `*param` refusal is the same bargain at the
  smallest possible grain.

RESEARCH METHOD (recorded 2026-08-03 after several wrong assertions)
  Asserting a method is absent after grepping ONE class is how three
  lessons got written wrong. The order that works:
      1. context_compass/system_docs/src_components_index.md  (line ranges)
      2. the named range in src_components.md                 (the claim)
      3. the source                                           (the truth)
  Docs surfaced things no grep would have: that refusal is a return
  value, that memory is a push model on RiftSpace, that campaign=None
  means inherit. Grep confirms; it does not survey.

  ADDENDUM AFTER THE FIRST RUN - AND IT IS THE MORE USEFUL HALF.
  Reading the source of a CALL tells you what the call does. It does not
  tell you WHAT THE DEFAULTS AROUND IT ARE, and both first-run failures
  were exactly that gap:
      - `_validate_target_frame_names` reads perfectly innocent. The bug
        was 200 lines away in a defaults dict: allowed_target_frame_names
        ships as ("default",), not as ().
      - `research_group_footprint` reads as a plain delegation. The bug
        was one frame deeper, in `_require_live_custody`.
  SO: when a lesson SETS UP a subsystem, read its defaults table, not
  just the verbs it calls. A default is a decision someone made and it is
  as much part of the contract as a signature.

  - RETRACTED 2026-08-03, SAME DAY IT WAS WRITTEN: "the canonical doc is
    stale on notch fan-out". IT IS NOT. The note is SEAM-SCOPED and the

    "Contracted borrowers are NOT yet fanned out HERE (owner-side only)".
    `_apply_notch` is the Spellbook's local switch; the fan-out lives one
    layer up in `Conduit.notch_spell`. Both statements are true at their
    own layer. The author read the doc's paraphrase of the seam, found
    fan-out code at the VERB, and called the doc wrong - without reading
    `_apply_notch` itself, where the qualifier is.
    ALSO UNRESOLVED AND NOT CLAIMED EITHER WAY: the limitation says "a
    notch on a SHARED index", and `shared` is cluster vocabulary
    (`ConduitCluster.get_shared_spells` -> owner_id -> {SpellIndex}), not
    contract-borrow vocabulary. The two fan-out calls at the verb handle
    LINKED peers and INDEX-LINK receivers. Whether cluster-shared indices
    are covered was never checked, so the limitation may be entirely
    current. Do not repeat the claim without reading the cluster path.
    LESSON: a scoped statement read out of its scope becomes a false one.
  - NO PUBLIC DOOR FOR REACH ENUMERATION (2026-08-03, lesson 13). Both
    `Rift.list_accessible_non_nexus_frame_names()` and the Nexus-level
    `list_accessible_non_nexus_frame_names(rift_id)` are marked
    `Internal` in their own docstrings. They are the best AIX door in the
    subsystem - they run BOTH attachment gates filtered by the rift's
    space type, so an agent can survey its reach instead of discovering
    a boundary by crossing it. An agent that cannot enumerate must probe,
    and probing an authority boundary is precisely what the rest of this
    design is built to avoid. Lesson 13 uses it and says plainly that it
    is Internal-marked rather than teaching it as public surface.
  - THE DEFAULT ALLOW-LIST IS A ONE-NAME TUPLE, NOT EMPTY.
    `allowed_target_frame_names` ships as ("default",). Because the check
    is skipped when the tuple is falsy, an EMPTY list means "unrestricted"
    - so the shipped value is the tight end of the dial, not the loose
    one. Worth a doc line somewhere prominent: the first thing anyone
    does with a rift is point it at a frame they named themselves, and
    the refusal message ("not allowed by Nexus policy") does not hint
    that a default allow-list is what they collided with.
  - `Conduit.transaction` ABORTS ON `Exception`, NOT ON `BaseException`
    (2026-08-03, lesson 16). The context manager is try/except/else, so
    a KeyboardInterrupt, SystemExit, or a GeneratorExit from the
    surrounding frame leaves the window OPEN with its claims held -
    which under a bounded-wait plane means other requests wait out the
    full `max_transaction_wait_time_in_seconds` for a session nobody is
    driving. Narrow, but the plane's own cleanup notes say a resisting
    session must not prevent teardown, so the intent is clearly that
    windows close. Worth a `finally` or an explicit BaseException arm.
    NOT pinned by a probe yet - raising BaseException inside an example
    would take the example runner with it.
  - SPELL IDS ARE PROCESS-WIDE AND THE FRAME IS NOT IN THE FINGERPRINT.
    Identical bindings in two frames COLLIDE. Every multi-frame lesson
    here passes binding_name= or spellframe= for that reason. It is the
    single most common way a working example goes red when copied.

SOURCE FIXES MADE ALONGSIDE THIS TIER (2026-08-03)

  1. THE HUSK BUG IN THE RESET DOORS - MutationResearch, then Crystallizer.
     SYMPTOM: `test_the_host_is_keyword_only` went red with
     `AttributeError: object has no attribute '_cleaned'` raised from
     inside `_reset_singleton_for_tests` itself.
     CAUSE: `__new__` publishes the singleton BEFORE `__init__` runs, and
     a construction that fails on the SIGNATURE (positional `aether`)
     fires its TypeError before `__init__`. `Cleanable.__slots__` is
     `['_cleaned']` and the flag is assigned in `__init__`, so the
     published husk has the slot UNSET - reading it raises rather than
     returning a default. The reset door died on the exact object it
     exists to clear.
     THE TEST HAD ALREADY PREDICTED THIS in its own comment: "a signature
     TypeError fires before `__init__` runs, so the body's rollback never
     executes and `__new__`'s published instance is left installed. The
     class's own reset door is what clears it." The door just could not.
     FOUR DOORS, THREE IMPLEMENTATIONS, WHICH IS HOW IT SURVIVED:
       Nexus            try/except AttributeError/finally - husk-safe
       Crystallizer     `not instance.cleaned`   - LATENT, same hole
       MutationResearch `not instance._cleaned`  - the one that fired
       Aether           try/finally, NO except
     THE REAL FIX WAS SMALLER THAN THE FIRST ATTEMPT (owner ruling):
     DELETE THE LIVENESS CHECK ENTIRELY. Every one of the four
     `cleanup()` methods already guards its own `_cleaned` flag and
     returns early, so a caller-side "is it clean yet" test was pure
     redundancy - and it was the redundancy that crashed, because it read
     a slot a husk does not have. A reset door does not need to know
     whether the thing is live. It cleans and it clears.
     ALL FOUR ARE NOW ONE SHAPE, verified by AST rather than by eye:
       clean unconditionally -> swallow the husk AttributeError ->
       clear `_instance` / `_initialized`
     Aether included: it keeps propagating real cleanup failures (its
     documented contract) and no longer dies on a husk. The "divergence"
     recorded here earlier was not a divergence to preserve - it was
     three copies of the same avoidable check, and the author had added
     a fourth before being told to stop.

  29 reading_your_own_recorded_code (THE CRYSTAL WELL - the code your
     world RECORDED, at four grains, plus the one comparison law that
     makes any of it trustworthy. Expert 04 said diffs are derived never
     stored; this is what they are derived FROM.
     FOUR GRAINS, and they are not four ways to do one thing:
     research_source = the whole module WORLD; research_module = ONE
     module as a one-call DOSSIER (text, fingerprint, path, deps BOTH
     ways, exports, drift - so you stop hand-joining five reads);
     research_parts = the INVENTORY, which needs no names up front and is
     what you reach for before you know what is in there; research_part =
     the lookup for when you do.
     THE COMPARISON LAW IS THE POINT: research_part_diff compares
     RECORDED MATERIAL ONLY and never the live disk. Not caution -
     correctness. Both sides of a version comparison would read the SAME
     present-day file, so a disk-backed diff reports `no change` between
     two genuinely different versions and is confidently wrong about
     both. The record is the only place two versions exist at once.
     Diff material drinks BOTH carriers (synthetic first, user-retained
     filling gaps) so it speaks the full module either way.
     IMPACT STAYS MODULE-GRAIN deliberately: a part's honest radius IS
     its module's radius, because nothing imports half a file.
     CUSTODY REFUSES LOUD and the lesson catches it and says so - a
     silent empty read is indistinguishable from `this world has no
     code`, which is the one answer that is never true.
     COVERAGE: this single lesson exercises 11 research commands, 10 of
     them previously untouched by any lesson, lifting the tier from
     15/34 to 25/34 of the codegen room's research family.)

ARC I COMPLETE (lessons 30-32) - the record as an EDITABLE instrument.
  Arc G made the record readable; this arc makes it something you
  reorganise, compose into, and interrogate at subsystem grain.

  30 COMPOSING A VERSION IN THE WORKSHOP - the half of a merge that
     `join` refuses to do. Expert 23 said it outright ("compose in the
     codegen workshop, register the multi-parent result, then join") and
     this is that workshop. research_synthesize splices named top-level
     parts from a donor into a base and returns a CANDIDATE - nothing
     executes, binds or records.
     THE SPLIT IS THE THESIS: a record that merged content FOR you would
     be guessing about your source, so melder separates composing (yours)
     from booking the outcome (the record's).
     TWO THINGS THAT LOOK LIKE BUGS AND ARE NOT, both worth the lesson's
     space: a REDISCOVERY DOES NOT CONSUME THE STAMP (identical content
     re-entering is not your candidate arriving, so it re-stages
     untouched); and THE STAMP SURVIVES UNTIL USED OR CLEARED - it is
     ambient, not attached to a call, and no scope ends it. That is why
     research_clear_staged_ancestry exists: abandon a composition without
     it and the next innocent bind inherits parents it never had.
     AND AN UNKNOWN DIFF STRATEGY IS NOT REROUTED - the room surfaces the
     engine's KeyError rather than quietly answering a different
     question than the one asked.

  31 ORGANISING LANES AFTER THE FACT - attach / detach / archive, the
     three verbs for when you got the shape wrong the first time.
     ANCESTRY IS ORGANISATION, NOT CONTENT: all three move where a lane
     SAYS it came from; none copies, moves or deletes a version. That
     separation is what makes reorganising cheap - a wrong anchor is a
     wrong LABEL, not lost work.
     ATTACH IS ALL-OR-NOTHING and refuses before taking a lock, because
     the anchor is the one fact a later join reasons about; a
     "anchor to whatever the tip is" shorthand would let you record a
     different anchor than you meant.
     DETACH IS NOT A DELETE. A detached lane still joins, but DIVERGENTLY
     BY DEFINITION - no anchor means nothing for the tip to agree with -
     so it needs the same explicit force=True supersede.
     AND THE DEFAULT LANE NEVER ARCHIVES: register_spell with no lane
     records THERE, so a set that archived it could not serve its own
     default. Checked at the door, not discovered later.

  32 A SUBSYSTEM'S BLAST RADIUS - the two questions you actually have
     about a composition (expert 14) once you have one.
     IMPACT IS A UNION WITH CLOSURE MATH, NOT A SUM: it merges every
     member's radius then splits INTERNAL vs OUTBOUND. The closure
     fraction is the number that matters - high closure is a subsystem
     you can change on its own terms; low closure is a subsystem in name
     only, whose edges are really everyone else's problem. It also lifts
     to composition grain, so "what else does this hit" is answerable in
     subsystem vocabulary rather than as a flat list of spells.
     DRIFT IS SOURCE_DRIFT NARROWED TO THE FOOTPRINT, and the narrowing
     is the point: whole-world drift on a real repository is mostly other
     people's churn, so the counts are recomputed over this subsystem's
     modules only.
     THE FOOTPRINT IS HONEST ABOUT WHAT IT CANNOT SEE - a member whose
     custody is unknown reports as unknown rather than silently
     contributing nothing. A shadow with a hole in it that claimed to be
     complete would be worse than no shadow.
     AND COMPOSITIONS STAY INFORMATIONAL: pinned by reference, no custody
     crystal, gates nothing, never executes - which is exactly why these
     questions are cheap to ask.
     COVERAGE: closes the codegen room's research family at 34/34.

ARC J (lesson 33) - WHAT THE GENERATED THING ACTUALLY IS.
  33 WHAT A SYNTHETIC MODULE ACTUALLY IS. Lessons 26, 27, 29, 30 and 32
     all MAKE synthetic modules. None of them said what one IS, and the
     tier shipped five lessons deep into codegen without ever defining
     its central object. This closes that.
     A SYNTHETIC MODULE IS A REAL MODULE WITH NO FILE - a live ModuleType
     subclass carrying its own source and hash, registered behind a
     meta-path finder so plain `import` resolves it. Its source IS the
     record, so there is no file to go stale.
     FOUR STATES, NONE INFERRED FROM ANOTHER: registration, import-hook
     install, publication, execution. `materialize_codegen` composes all
     four, and it PUBLISHES BEFORE IT EXECUTES on purpose - that is how
     importlib treats real modules, so a circular import sees a
     partially-initialised module rather than a missing one.
     CUSTODY IS THE REAL SUBJECT. Bind classifies every module it walks
     through FOUR authority classes, FIRST match wins:
       synthetic_module - claims by OBJECT IDENTITY, never path, because
         a path rule would misclassify it. No disk read. NO fingerprint
         claim; its rebuild payload already carries source_sha256.
       user_source - path under configured roots. THE ONLY FINGERPRINT
         CUSTODIAN, and that is the trust boundary that makes drift
         detectable at all.
       site_package - descends and reads, claims NOTHING. You did not
         write it, so its changing is not your bug.
       unknown - the ONLY class that does not descend. An honest leaf, so
         the manifest never implies a more complete dependency picture
         than the source supports.
     SO "CAN THIS DRIFT" IS ANSWERED BY CUSTODY, NOT BY CHANCE. Only user
     source is fingerprinted, so only user source can be caught changing.
     A synthetic module cannot drift - not unchecked, but because its
     text IS the record. That is why a recorded row reports drifted=None:
     there is no second copy to disagree with.
     AND BIND FORMATS BOTH INTO ONE CRYSTAL. No synthetic crystal, no
     file crystal - one flat module inventory, four kind-partitions over
     it, and root_module_kind naming the lane the root took. The KIND is
     DATA IN the crystal, which is exactly why a world can mix generated
     and hand-written code and checkpoint as one thing.
     ON POINTING AT INTERNALS: SyntheticModule, the custody strategies
     and SpellCrystal are all AGENT_ACCESS: internal - "read it to
     understand the runtime, do not drive it directly". 33 NAMES them
     because you cannot reason about your own world without knowing they
     exist, and drives only the public surface.

THE HAND-TYPED-CLASS CORRECTION (2026-08-04) - 29, 30 AND 32
  A run put 30 RED and the owner asked why no lesson used raw codegen.
  Measured: of lessons 26-32 only 26 and 27 drove the authoring surface;
  28-32 used classes typed into the example file. In THREE of them that
  was not cosmetic, because the recorded unit is the MODULE:
    30 - two classes in one file share one module, so base_text ==
      donor_text, every selection was a part replaced by itself, and the
      "added" action was UNREACHABLE. The lesson could not demonstrate
      its own subject. It now generates two module worlds and asserts
      BOTH actions.
    29 - both versions shared one module snapshot, so every part_diff
      compared identical bytes. It was GREEN and vacuous, which is worse
      than red. It also asked for `quote` as a top-level function when
      `quote` was a method; part_view returns `found: False` rather than
      raising, so the miss was invisible. Now two generated modules with
      a real top-level `quote`, and the method miss is a LABELLED
      teaching moment instead of an accident.
    32 - three members in one file gave a ONE-module footprint, and a
      union over one module is not a union. Now three module worlds.
  THE LESSON UNDER THE LESSON, and it inverts the obvious assumption:
  GENERATED SOURCE IS THE RELIABLE INPUT, not the exotic one. "Synthetic
  module sources are ALWAYS harvested; user module text rides the opt-in
  retention lane." Hand-typed example classes are the FRAGILE choice for
  anything that reads recorded material.

THE KIND-AWARE DIFF DEFAULT (2026-08-05) - 30 AND 32 NOW TEACH BOTH HALVES
  Found by reading `research_diff` in full instead of extracting its
  signature. 30 previously said "the room defaults to `structural`", which
  is true for spells and WRONG as a general statement.
  THE ACTUAL BRANCH: with no strategy the room asks
  `is_composition(left) and is_composition(right)`. If they are NOT both
  compositions it pins "structural" and calls down. If they ARE, it passes
  NO strategy at all and lets the engine's own "members" default answer.
  One verb, two vocabularies, selected by KIND rather than one fallback.
  AND A DEFAULT IS A KINDNESS FOR SILENCE, NEVER AN OVERRIDE: the moment a
  caller names a strategy it travels down untouched, and an unknown name
  surfaces the engine's KeyError (BUG-044 law, stated in the docstring).
  30 states the law and demonstrates the SPELL half. 32 now demonstrates
  the COMPOSITION half, which it can do honestly because `recompose` gives
  it a second composition to compare against.

  AND 32 GAINED THE RECOMPOSE LAW WITH IT. Evolving a composition is
  ADD/REMOVE, not replacement - "unlisted members are retained" - so
  dropping one member is a one-word ask rather than a re-declaration of the
  roster. The previous composition is untouched, because identity is
  content-addressed over the members: a different roster is a DIFFERENT
  composition, not an edited one. That is why `members` is the right
  default vocabulary for a composition pair - the useful question about two
  subsystems is which MEMBERS changed, and each moved pair descends into
  the spell grains on the agent's NEXT call.

AMENDMENT TO LESSON 06 (2026-08-04) - TWO STALE CLAIMS, ONE REAL GAP
  06's ladder table named `Nexus.enable()`. THERE IS NO `enable` ON
  NEXUS - nexus.py defines `activate` / `deactivate` and zero `def
  enable`. The SUBSTANCE of the claim survives (nexus.py:838 finalizes
  the installed configuration on its way through, which the other three
  roots do not do for you, so "three to one" still holds); only the verb
  name had drifted. Corrected in place.
  THE REAL GAP: NexusConfigurationBuilder was the last public root name
  no lesson referenced. Nexus was once the one root of four with NO
  builder; it now carries all three exits, so 06's generosity table was
  simply out of date. Added there rather than as a new lesson, because 06
  IS the configuration lesson and the builder completes its own table.
  THE THREE LAWS IT CARRIES: exits are ONE-SHOT ownership transfers that
  consume the builder (one owner at each step); the builder's activate()
  marks the CONFIGURATION active and the Nexus is still off (two
  objects, two bits, unbent by the new shape); and build() earns its
  place precisely BECAUSE the builder mirrors only one knob while the
  configuration carries the wide surface - a frozen-only builder would
  have made frame allow/deny lists unreachable through it.

  FINDING FOR ANOTHER TIER, NOT ACTED ON: advanced 08's PROSE is stale
  the same way - its code calls nexus.activate(config) but its narration
  still says "enable" throughout ("nothing is wired until you pass it to
  enable()", "enable seals it for you") and its SURFACE line reads
  `create_configuration, enable, disable`. Advanced is not this epic's
  lane; recorded here so whoever holds it does not have to rediscover it.

THE TIER'S OWN SHAPE, NOW THAT IT IS DONE
  It opens with a COLD BOOT (01) and closes with a document that answers
  BEFORE any boot at all (18). In between it goes: record what changed
  (03-06), let an agent write into a running world (07-15), let several
  agents mutate it at once (16), and prepare a swap without taking it
  (17). Read in order, the tier is a widening circle of who is allowed
  to change what - and every widening is paid for with a new way to
  REFUSE precisely. That is the through-line worth naming out loud:
  melder buys concurrency and agency with precision of refusal, never
  with permissiveness.

  - boot melds (owner epic 2026-07-20, unassigned): conjure-time warm-up
    recipe riding the bind signature into checkpoints.
  (the self-documenting package landed as lesson 18)

# UX_and_AIX_experiences (AGENTS.md)

Purpose: the living exploration of how HUMANS (UX) and AGENTS (AIX) use melder,
tiered beginner -> intermediate -> advanced -> expert (matched to the
README ladder, owner ruling 2026-07-22). Every example is written
against `import melder as md` ONLY - any example forced to reach a deep path is,
by definition, an init-surface gap and must be recorded on the owning epic.

Layout:
- 01_beginner/      first-contact + registration: bind, SpellBinder fluent, meld, lifecycles,
                    hooks, disposal, frames, errors, agent first-read.
                    TIER LAW: static conjure only - no dynamic, no Nexus, no MutationResearch,
                    no spellspaces. Existences: unique, many, unique_per_conduit
                    ONLY (lineage/spellspace -> tier 02; cluster -> tier 03).
                    DESIGN PRINCIPLE: teach a 4B-model agent with a 64k window
                    to be USEFUL - shared/fresh/scoped, dict-style frame ADDRESSING (frames are
                    grouping/contract keys, not dicts), typed
                    melds, Protocols, one bootstrap function. Fun and simple
                    beats complete.
- 02_intermediate/  linking + dynamic mode + configurations (owner fence:
                    NO Nexus, NO MutationResearch, NO crystallizer, and NO
                    AethericFrame objects - substrate stays invisible; the
                    _dynamic_world helper is a black box by design)
- 03_advanced/      frames as worlds, static rooms, clusters, deep overrides
- 04_expert/        AR rooms, transactions, checkpoints, governed mutation, external DB meshes

Laws:
- Examples are RUNNABLE scripts (3.14t) with a main() and honest printed asserts.
- Each file header states TIER / GOAL / SURFACE EXERCISED (the md.* names used).
- Examples never import melder submodule paths. md.* or it does not exist.
- Findings (gaps, awkward verbs, missing exports) go on the tier's epic ticket,
  then flow into the init composition story - examples are the evidence.

Tickets: context_compass/tickets/epics/2026-07-19_ux_aix_{tier}_experience_epic.md

## Verification harness

pytest_examples/ runs every example plus contract probes on 3.14t:

    pytest UX_and_AIX_experiences/pytest_examples -v

LAW (2026-07-19, after the bind(**kwargs) miss): examples may only assert
behavior VERIFIED in source or PROVEN by a probe row. Uncertain contracts get
a probe here first; the probe's printed outcome then hardens the example.

## Curriculum arc: categories (owner-directed 2026-07-20)

- The category idea threads the tiers. BEGINNER 25: spellframes as
  categories - organize spells WITHIN one world; (category, name) is the
  full address. INTERMEDIATE 26: conduits as categories - a wider frame;
  each category is its own world with an OWNER, and permissions +
  contracts + links set the resolution conditions at the category
  boundary. Same idea, organized differently: manage who owns what.

## Discovered runtime laws (harness run 3, 2026-07-20)

- SHARING IS A PULL: `X.add_spell_to_contract(spell_id=S, conduit=Y)` means
  "X pulls S from Y" - the conduit NAMED in the call must OWN the spell
  (ConduitWard._check_spell_if_eligible ownership check). Owner-pushes are
  refused with "not owned by this conduit".
- ONE ACTIVE SPELL PER SIGNATURE: the frame-wide LookupContainer claims one
  (frame_key, binding_name) per spell - collection-DI providers sharing a
  spellframe MUST carry distinct binding_names.
- CLUSTER STORE = ELECTED LEADER: unique_per_conduit_cluster melds hard-error
  ("cluster_creations is disabled") until `cluster.elect_leader(conduit_id)`
  runs; membership alone does not arm the team store.
- ONE BOOK, ONE CONJURE holds for lineage too: a second family is a second
  book; lineages GROW via create_lesser_conduit, never via re-conjure.
- SPELLCONTRACT ORDER OF OPERATIONS (owner ruling 2026-07-20, "the code is
  fine"): per dependency edge - 1) conjure the PROVIDER conduit, 2) conjure
  the CONSUMER conduit, 3) link() only AFTER both are built, 4) the consumer
  pulls the provider spell into the contract, 5) MELD after the fact - the
  meld completes the late binding for that world's products. Chains assemble
  edge by edge in dependency order. Skipping the cycle (e.g. never melding a
  middle world before handing its spell downstream) is USAGE ERROR: the
  un-melded consumer constructs with its Python default (the descriptor) -
  that is the misuse outcome, not a runtime gap.
- NORMAL CODE ONLY (owner ruling 2026-07-20): curriculum code never pulls
  mediator transactions into user flow - no transaction("link", ...) windows
  around add_spell_to_contract (the verb SELF-ADMITS its own transaction,
  conduit.py:4956) and no validate_contracts_and_define ceremony in lessons.
  The user surface is link / add_spell_to_contract / meld.
- HARNESS IMPORT LAW: spec-loaded lesson modules must be registered in
  sys.modules BEFORE exec_module - scan lessons look themselves up via
  sys.modules[__name__].

## Discovered runtime laws (harness runs 1-2, 2026-07-19)

- Callable spells (functions, lambdas, methods) are ALWAYS unique; lambdas
  additionally REQUIRE a binding_name. Fresh-per-meld factories are CLASSES
  bound "many".
- THE ADDRESS LAW: every spell lives at exactly one (frame_key, binding_key)
  address - frame_key = spellframe else normalized spell name; binding_key =
  binding_name else the default slot. Public positional strings and `spell=`
  strings are human SpellNames; classes/Protocols remain supported; opaque SHA
  identity uses explicit `spell_id=`. Human-name/class forms derive the frame key
  from the NAME (so they miss framed binds), and a bind with binding_name answers
  only when the meld carries the same binding_name. binding_name alone is refused.
- Spell NAMES are unique per book at conjure - CURRENT behavior refuses any
  name collision regardless of binding names, frames, or content SHA.
  DIVERGENCE FLAG: owner design intent (twice stated) is SHA256 content
  matching with binding-name disambiguation; DuplicateSpellNameStrategy
  ignores the disambiguators its own error message recommends. Tracked as a
  runtime bug candidate on the beginner epic. Until fixed: subclass-per-role
  (24) and collection-as-spell registries (33) are the working patterns.
- One book conjures ONE conduit ever (RuntimeError on the second); scopes are
  lesser conduits, extra roots are extra books.
- Unregistered meld raises one stable KeyError. Same-spell double-bind is
  refused at BIND time (RuntimeError).
- bind(**kwargs) is the hook channel and SWALLOWS unknown keys silently
  (flagged as a fail-fast design question); constructor config rides
  factories, prebuilt instances, or meld(override={...}).
- Disposal (disposal_method_names) fires at conduit.cleanup().
- Harness isolation: reset the Aether singleton + rebind Spellbook/
  Conduit._aether around every test (component-suite fixture, verbatim).

"""
Per-test world isolation for the example harness.

WHY THIS RESETS FIVE SINGLETONS AND NOT ONE
-------------------------------------------
This fixture used to reset only `Aether`, mirroring the component suite's
frame-truth fixture. That was sufficient while examples stayed below the
substrate - beginner, intermediate and advanced never touch the hosted
roots. EXPERT DOES, and the omission surfaced as a real red on the
2026-08-04 owner run.

`test_expert_probes.py` already carries the correct fixture and states the
reason exactly: "All five carry process-wide state; without the reset one
row's checkpoints, profiles or research lanes surface in the next row."
The PROBES had that isolation; the EXAMPLES did not, so expert lessons ran
against whatever record the previous lesson left behind.

WHAT THAT LOOKED LIKE, so the next reader recognises it
-------------------------------------------------------
Expert 27 seals a checkpoint, tears the runtime down, and unfolds the
record into a fresh root. It failed at admission with

    owning spellbook '01K...' is not in this bundle; the custody cannot
    bind ... nothing was built

and the run reported SEVENTY-SIX cached checkpoint ids in a session where
that lesson mints exactly one. `Aether` was being reset between examples
while `Crystallizer` was not, so each lesson's frames were cleaned out from
under a record that survived them - leaving custody rows whose owning
spellbook had been evicted, in a profile shared by every example in the
file. A whole-world load then folds that shared chain and refuses.

THE ORDER MATTERS
-----------------
Reset the hosted roots BEFORE `Aether`, then construct a fresh `Aether`
and rebind the class seams. `Aether` boots the hosted singletons, so
resetting it first and the children second would leave the fresh root
holding children that are about to be discarded.
"""
import pytest

from melder import Aether, Conduit, Crystallizer, MutationResearch, Nexus
from melder.aether.spellbook.spellbook import Spellbook


@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
def reset_world_per_example() -> None:
    """
    Purpose:
        Every example runs in a FRESH world - no shared frames, no
        root-conduit name collisions, and no inherited record.

    Contract:
        - Resets the four process-wide roots plus `Aether`, matching
          `test_expert_probes.py`'s fixture rather than the narrower
          Aether-only reset this file used to carry.
        - Runs before AND after every example, so a lesson cannot leak
          into its neighbour in either direction.
        - Rebinds the `Spellbook`/`Conduit` class seams to the fresh
          `Aether`, which is what makes the new root the one those types
          resolve against.
    """
    def _fresh() -> None:
        MutationResearch._reset_singleton_for_tests()
        Crystallizer._reset_singleton_for_tests()
        Nexus._reset_singleton_for_tests()
        Aether._reset_singleton_for_tests()
        aether = Aether()
        Spellbook._aether = aether
        Conduit._aether = aether

    _fresh()
    yield
    _fresh()

CONTENT SHA256: c1e8ecd8b512db5e3db0e63c0826ed549f08cff5f5fafca034a77918ddc722b5

"""
EXAMPLE: shared_framewide_spellbook_configuration

ONE SpellbookConfiguration owned by the FRAME, adopted by every book on
it. No config passed to anybody after the first publish.

WHY THIS FILE LIVED BESIDE THE PROBES: step 2 needed the frame posture,
and no public door reached it - so the file could not obey the tier rule
that lessons import `melder as md` only. That condition is now MET.
configure_aether_frame() accepts shared_framewide_spellbook_configuration
as of 2026-08-03, step 2 below is one public call, and this file is
READY TO MOVE INTO 02_intermediate/ on the owner's numbering call.

WHY THE SWITCH AND THE PUBLISH ARE ONE CALL
configure_aether_frame() is not a pure posture setter: it writes posture,
then FREEZES the rich spellbook configuration and binds it to the frame.
So the policy must be shaped BEFORE the call, and the switch travels IN
it - posture is applied first inside the method, so the bind that follows
in the same call already sees shared=True. Flipping the switch in an
earlier call would freeze the config before step 2 could shape it.

THE FOUR STEPS
  1. build the first book - this mints the frame and its posture
  2. shape the policy on that first book's config - this object is about
     to become the whole frame's policy
  3. ONE PUBLIC CALL: configure_aether_frame(
         shared_framewide_spellbook_configuration=True) sets the switch on
     the frame-owned posture, freezes the policy, and binds it to the
     frame. Must happen BEFORE the frame's first conjure: conjure binds and
     FREEZES the posture (aetheric_frame.py:667-726) and the setter is
     refused once frozen (aetheric_frame_configuration.py:653). conjure()
     is the other publish door (spellbook_creation_system.py:296-300) -
     FIRST ONE WINS
  4. every book built after that ADOPTS the frame-owned object at
     construction and comes back locked
"""
import melder as md


class Alpha:
    pass


class Beta:
    pass


class Gamma:
    pass


FRAME = "one-config-world"


def main() -> None:
    # ---- step 1: first book mints the frame and its posture -----------
    first = md.Spellbook(aetheric_frame=FRAME)

    # A book that exists BEFORE publication. Watch it converge in step 5.
    early = md.Spellbook(aetheric_frame=FRAME)
    assert early.get_configuration() is not first.get_configuration()

    # ---- step 2: shape the policy the whole frame will run under -----
    # Shape it FIRST. The publish call below freezes this object.
    policy = first.get_configuration()
    policy.set_property("phase_scheduler_workers_per_spellbook", 1)

    # ---- step 3: THE SWITCH AND THE PUBLISH, IN ONE PUBLIC CALL ------
    # The posture object is frame-owned; every book on the frame holds
    # this same reference, so the switch set through `first` is set for
    # the frame. configure_aether_frame applies posture BEFORE it freezes
    # and binds, so the bind in this same call already sees shared=True.
    # disposal/disposal_method_names are idempotent set-once keys and
    # load_default_dictionary() already set them on an auto-minted book,
    # so pass None. system_state=None leaves the mode alone.
    first.configure_aether_frame(
        system_state=None,
        disposal=None,
        disposal_method_names=None,
        shared_framewide_spellbook_configuration=True,
    )
    assert first.is_configuration_locked() is True
    print("published:", policy is first.get_configuration())

    # ---- step 4: ADOPTION - nothing passed, nothing configured -------
    second = md.Spellbook(aetheric_frame=FRAME)
    assert second.get_configuration() is policy
    assert second.is_configuration_locked() is True
    assert second.get_configuration().get_property(
        "phase_scheduler_workers_per_spellbook"
    ) == 1
    print("second book adopted the frame's config, locked, never asked")

    # Handing a DIFFERENT config to a later book is refused outright.
    try:
        md.Spellbook(
            aetheric_frame=FRAME,
            configuration=md.SpellbookConfiguration(FRAME),
        )
        raise AssertionError("expected the frame to refuse a rival config")
    except RuntimeError as error:
        print("rival config refused:", error)

    # ---- step 5: the pre-existing book CONVERGES at its own conjure ---
    # It still holds its private config right now...
    assert early.get_configuration() is not policy
    early.bind(spell=Gamma, existence="unique")
    early.conjure(name="early")
    # ...and conjure swapped it onto the frame-owned object and cleaned
    # up the local one (spellbook.py:5626-5650).
    assert early.get_configuration() is policy
    assert early.is_configuration_locked() is True
    print("pre-existing book converged onto the shared config at conjure")

    # ---- everything runs under the one policy ------------------------
    first.bind(spell=Alpha, existence="unique")
    second.bind(spell=Beta, existence="unique")
    conduit_one = first.conjure(name="first")
    conduit_two = second.conjure(name="second")
    assert isinstance(conduit_one.meld(spell=Alpha), Alpha)
    assert isinstance(conduit_two.meld(spell=Beta), Beta)
    print("three books, three worlds, ONE configuration object")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""
Runs every advanced example as a pytest row (same harness law as the
other tiers). Run on 3.14t:

    pytest UX_and_AIX_experiences/pytest_examples -v
"""
import importlib.util
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

EXAMPLES = sorted(
    (Path(__file__).parent.parent / "03_advanced").glob("[0-9]*.py")
)


def _load(path: Path):
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(
        "ux_adv_example_" + path.stem, path
    )
    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    # Import law (run 3): register BEFORE exec - lessons may look
    # themselves up via sys.modules[__name__].
    sys.modules[spec.name] = module
    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
    return module


@pytest.mark.parametrize("path", EXAMPLES, ids=[p.stem for p in EXAMPLES])
def test_advanced_example_runs_green(path, capsys):
    module = _load(path)
    module.main()
    out = capsys.readouterr().out
    assert out.strip(), "examples narrate - silence means something broke"

"""
Advanced-tier contract probes. Run on 3.14t:

    pytest UX_and_AIX_experiences/pytest_examples/test_advanced_probes.py -v
"""
import melder as md
import pytest

from melder import Aether, Conduit, Crystallizer, Nexus
from melder.aether.spellbook.spellbook import Spellbook
from melder.aether.aether import Aether


@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
def reset_aether_world() -> None:
    """Per-row world reset.

    FIVE classes in src/melder expose `_reset_singleton_for_tests`:
    Aether, AetherUtilitySystem, Crystallizer, MutationResearch, Nexus.
    This fixture resets the two THIS TIER touches - Aether (every row) and
    Nexus (arc B). The rows below activate Aether and enable Nexus, which
    are process-wide flips; without the reset they would leak forward and
    make later rows pass or fail depending on collection order.

    Crystallizer joined the reset with arc E (lessons 17-18): checkpoint
    ids and cached checkpoints are process-wide, so without it one row's
    checkpoints show up in the next row's list_checkpoint_ids().

    NOT reset here, deliberately:
      - AetherUtilitySystem: Aether resolves its logger provider through
        it, and resetting it underneath a live Aether is a wider blast
        radius than these rows need.
      - MutationResearch: untouched by advanced - it is EXPERT material.
    """
    def _fresh() -> None:
        Crystallizer._reset_singleton_for_tests()
        Nexus._reset_singleton_for_tests()
        Aether._reset_singleton_for_tests()
        aether = Aether()
        Spellbook._aether = aether
        Conduit._aether = aether

    _fresh()
    yield
    _fresh()


class Payload:
    pass


def test_probe_frames_isolate_instances_but_not_identity():
    """Lesson 02 contract, REWRITTEN 2026-08-03. This row used to pin the
    README claim that "two frames bind the SAME class with zero
    collision". EPIC-2026-08-02 S2 retired that: a spell_id hashes the
    bind fingerprint and the FRAME IS NOT IN IT, so identical bindings on
    different frames mint one id and the second conjure is refused.

    What survived is the half that was always the real point - once the
    BINDINGS differ, `unique` is one instance PER FRAME and the wall
    holds. Both halves are asserted here so neither can drift alone."""
    book_a = Spellbook(aetheric_frame="probe-tenant-a")
    book_b = Spellbook(aetheric_frame="probe-tenant-b")
    book_a.bind(spell=Payload, existence="unique", binding_name="tenant-a")
    book_b.bind(spell=Payload, existence="unique", binding_name="tenant-b")
    a = book_a.conjure().meld(spell=Payload, binding_name="tenant-a")
    b = book_b.conjure().meld(spell=Payload, binding_name="tenant-b")
    assert a is not b
    print("frame isolation pinned: same class, two worlds, two singletons")


def test_probe_posture_public_door_then_freeze():
    """Lesson 03 contract: configure_aether_frame(system_state="dynamic")
    before any conjure -> plain conjures inherit and link; after the
    first conjure froze the posture, reconfiguring refuses."""
    book = Spellbook(aetheric_frame="probe-ops")
    book.bind(spell=Payload, existence="unique")
    book.configure_aether_frame(system_state="dynamic", disposal=None,
                                disposal_method_names=None)
    root = book.conjure(name="probe-ops-root")
    peer = Spellbook(aetheric_frame="probe-ops").conjure(name="probe-ops-peer")
    assert root.link(peer) is True
    with pytest.raises(Exception) as refused:
        book.configure_aether_frame(system_state="automatic", disposal=None,
                                    disposal_method_names=None)
    print("post-freeze reconfigure refusal type:", type(refused.value).__name__)


def test_probe_devops_flags_gate_through_the_public_door():
    """RESOLVED (2026-08-03): the frame devops flags now have a public
    door. This row used to stage disable_linking through the book's
    PRIVATE retained posture because none existed; it now drives the same
    gate through configure_aether_frame and asserts the SAME refusal, so
    what it proves is that widening the door did not change the behaviour
    behind it. Note the two knobs travel in ONE call - system_state is
    applied first inside the method, which is what lets a single call move
    the world to dynamic and brake it at the same time."""
    book = Spellbook(aetheric_frame="probe-flags")
    book.bind(spell=Payload, existence="unique")
    book.configure_aether_frame(
        system_state="dynamic",
        disposal=None,
        disposal_method_names=None,
        disable_linking=True,
    )
    owner = book.conjure(dynamic=True, name="flag-owner")
    borrower = Spellbook(aetheric_frame="probe-flags").conjure(name="flag-borrower")
    with pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match="disabled"):
        owner.link(borrower)
    print("devops flag gate pinned through the PUBLIC door: link refused")


def test_probe_attach_logger_lifecycle():
    """Lesson 04 contract: melder boots silent; attach_logger attaches a

    import logging

    aether.attach_logger(logger)

    aether.enable_logging(logger)
    aether.attach_logger(None)

def test_probe_frame_posture_is_constructor_first():
    """Lesson 06 claim #1: this config cannot be built empty. Four values
    are REQUIRED keyword-only arguments. If a bare constructor ever starts
    working, the lesson's headline is wrong and this row goes red first."""
    with pytest.raises(TypeError):
        md.AethericFrameConfiguration()
    posture = md.AethericFrameConfiguration(
        origin_spellbook_id=None,
        system_state="automatic",
        ai_native_enabled=False,
        rift_enabled=False,
    )
    assert posture.system_state.name == "automatic"
    print("constructor-first pinned: 4 required kw-only values")


def test_probe_frame_posture_with_star_mutates_and_returns_self():
    """Lesson 06 claim #2: with_* is fluent in SHAPE ONLY. It mutates this
    object and returns SELF - never a clone. The frame's settlement law
    requires the RETAINED posture to be the bound one, so a copying with_*
    would be silently harmful rather than merely surprising."""
    posture = md.AethericFrameConfiguration(
        origin_spellbook_id=None,
        system_state="automatic",
        ai_native_enabled=False,
        rift_enabled=False,
    )
    returned = posture.with_system_caching_enabled(False)
    assert returned is posture
    assert posture.system_caching_enabled is False
    # presets follow the same law
    assert posture.dynamic_defaults() is posture
    assert posture.system_state.name == "dynamic"
    print("with_* and presets pinned: mutate-and-return-self, no clones")


def test_probe_frame_posture_validate_raises_rather_than_returning_false():
    """Lesson 06 claim #3: validate() RAISES. The bool return is a
    convention, not a verdict channel - a caller who writes
    `if not cfg.validate()` never runs. The semantic rule it enforces:
    ai_native_enabled requires system_state dynamic."""
    posture = md.AethericFrameConfiguration(
        origin_spellbook_id=None,
        system_state="automatic",
        ai_native_enabled=False,
        rift_enabled=False,
    )
    posture.with_ai_native(True)
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="dynamic"):
        posture.validate()
    posture.with_system_state("dynamic")
    assert posture.validate() is True
    print("validate pinned: raises on ai_native-without-dynamic, True after")


def test_probe_frame_posture_finalize_seals_same_instance():
    """Lesson 06 claim #4: finalize() freezes and returns THE SAME
    instance, and the freeze seals rather than clears - values survive."""
    posture = md.AethericFrameConfiguration(
        origin_spellbook_id=None,
        system_state="dynamic",
        ai_native_enabled=True,
        rift_enabled=False,
    )
    finalized = posture.finalize()
    assert finalized is posture
    with pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match="frozen"):
        posture.with_system_state("automatic")
    assert posture.system_state.name == "dynamic"
    assert posture.ai_native_enabled is True
    print("finalize pinned: same instance, frozen, values intact")


def test_probe_frame_posture_has_no_public_install_door_but_a_total_one():
    """THE GAP THIS ROW PINNED HAS CLOSED (2026-08-03), and the row is
    rewritten rather than deleted because BOTH halves still matter.

    STILL TRUE: md.AethericFrameConfiguration is exported from the public
    root and CANNOT BE INSTALLED FROM IT. Spellbook.__init__ takes
    (aetheric_frame, configuration, logger) where `configuration` is a
    SpellbookConfiguration. That is deliberate - the collaborator stays
    private.

    NO LONGER TRUE: that this left the posture unauthorable. The door
    carried 2 of 14 knobs; it now carries 14 of 14, so the capability is
    reachable while the object stays behind the facade. This row now pins
    TOTALITY - it goes RED if a posture builder is ever added without a
    matching parameter, which is the failure mode that created the gap in
    the first place."""
    import inspect
    parameters = inspect.signature(Spellbook.__init__).parameters
    assert "aetheric_frame_configuration" not in parameters
    annotation = parameters["configuration"].annotation
    assert "AethericFrameConfiguration" not in str(annotation)

    builders = {
        name[len("with_"):]
        for name, _ in inspect.getmembers(
            md.AethericFrameConfiguration, inspect.isfunction
        )
        if name.startswith("with_") and name != "with_defaults"
    }
    door = set(inspect.signature(Spellbook.configure_aether_frame).parameters)
    unreachable = builders - door
    assert not unreachable, f"posture knobs with no public door: {sorted(unreachable)}"
    assert {"rift_enabled", "ai_native", "disable_linking"}.issubset(door)
    print("posture door is TOTAL:", len(builders), "builders,",
          len(builders), "reachable; the object itself stays private")


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Lesson 07 - two doors, and the frozen/activated split
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def test_probe_both_config_doors_land_frozen_not_activated():
    """Lesson 07 claim: create_configuration().finalize() and
    create_configuration_builder().build() land on the SAME rung - frozen,
    NOT activated. If either door ever auto-activates, the ladder the
    lesson teaches is wrong."""
    aether = Aether()

    config = aether.create_configuration()
    assert config.frozen is False and config.activated is False
    assert config.with_defaults().finalize() is config
    assert config.frozen is True
    assert config.activated is False

    built = aether.create_configuration_builder().with_defaults().build()
    assert built.frozen is True
    assert built.activated is False
    assert built is not config
    print("both doors pinned: frozen is not activated")


def test_probe_config_activate_is_a_second_distinct_bit():
    """Lesson 07 headline: frozen and activated are TWO bits. Freezing
    sets one. activate() sets the other. Nothing sets both at once."""
    aether = Aether()
    config = aether.create_configuration().with_defaults().finalize()
    assert (config.frozen, config.activated) == (True, False)
    config.activate()
    assert (config.frozen, config.activated) == (True, True)
    print("two-bit split pinned: frozen then activated, never together")


def test_probe_aether_refuses_frozen_but_inactive_configuration():
    """Lesson 07 ORDERING RULE, pinned where it is safe to pin it.
    Aether's contract: "THE CONFIGURATION MUST BE ACTIVATED BEFORE AETHER
    CAN BE." This lives in the probe rather than the lesson because Aether
    is a process-wide singleton AND activate() installs the config BEFORE
    checking the activated bit - so even the refusing call mutates the
    world. The reset fixture owns a clean singleton; a lesson sharing an
    interpreter with 40 others does not."""
    aether = Aether()
    frozen_only = aether.create_configuration().with_defaults().finalize()
    assert frozen_only.activated is False
    with pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match="activated"):
        aether.activate(frozen_only)
    print("ordering rule pinned: aether refuses a merely-frozen config")


def test_probe_aether_comes_up_once_the_rungs_are_climbed_in_order():
    """The positive half of the ordering rule: rung 2 then rung 3 works."""
    aether = Aether()
    config = aether.create_configuration().with_defaults().finalize()
    config.activate()
    aether.activate(config)
    assert aether.activated is True
    print("ladder pinned: finalize -> config.activate -> aether.activate")
